packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (no connected text recovered)

Exposure statement
No proposed identification, title, author or earlier reading reached me in my context for this packet. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..008.jpg. One thing beyond the bare rules: I ran a single filtered file listing of the four packet directories (output restricted to PROMPT.md and image-*.jpg names) to learn how many images each holds; I did not open packet.json or anything else.

Layout survey (observation)
- image-001 (overview): a small limp-vellum-bound book, cover face, with colour checker and ruler (book about 11 cm wide). A rectangular parchment strip, darker and greyer than the cover, is pasted over the upper right of the cover next to the spine, roughly 3.5 cm wide and 6 cm tall, and wraps onto the spine.
- image-004 (overview): the same cover rotated 90 degrees; the strip is at lower right. In this orientation faint grey-brown horizontal bands cross the strip.
- image-007 (overview): the inside of the board/pastedown, heavily wormed, with a small parchment tab (the turn-in of the same or a similar strip) at upper left by the joint, about 2.5 cm wide.
- image-002, -003: native tiles of the strip as seen in image-001 (upper part, lower part; they overlap around the brown hole at the right edge).
- image-005, -006: native tiles of the strip as seen in image-004 (left part, right part).
- image-008: native tile of the inner tab seen in image-007.

What is visible of the script (observation)
- The strip carries writing, but it is either on the pasted-down side showing through, or abraded to a ghost. It appears as rows of blurred grey-brown smudges, not as strokes.
- In image-006 (the best view) I count about 9 to 10 rows of such smudges, evenly spaced, running the long way of the strip, i.e. perpendicular to the book's own text direction (the strip was applied sideways). Row spacing is roughly 2.5 to 3 mm by the ruler in image-005, so this is a small script. The rows seem to run the full width of the tile with no clear intercolumn; whether this is one column or part of one cannot be told from a 3.5 cm strip.
- In image-002 the same rows appear as vertical bands. No rubric, coloured initial, running title, underlining, or gloss is visible. A faint pink speck near the centre-left of image-002/-006 is too small to call a rubric.
- image-005: at upper left of the strip, two short darker marks (rows 2 and 3 from the top edge of the strip) that might be the ends of lines or offset ink; no letter can be resolved. A faint vertical stroke at centre right could be a ruled line or a fold.
- image-003: lower part of the strip; a few vertical grey streaks at lower left, more likely staining or ruling than letters.
- image-008 (inner tab): very faint horizontal rows, perhaps 8 to 10, visible as slightly darker bands in the right two-thirds of the tab; again no letter forms resolve. Lower part has a patch of white mould or fibre and worm damage.

Tentative interpretation (flagged as such)
- A reused manuscript strip serving as a spine/cover reinforcement, written in a small hand in long lines, text side probably facing down or rubbed away. I cannot determine language, script type, or whether the text is prose or verse.

Transcription
image-001: no text (overview).
image-002: lines 1-10 (counted as vertical bands, left to right) [illegible] throughout.
image-003: [illegible]; possibly no writing in this portion.
image-004: no legible text (overview).
image-005: lines 1-9 [illegible] throughout.
image-006: lines 1-10 [illegible] throughout.
image-007: no text (overview).
image-008: lines 1-c.10 [illegible] throughout.

I looked at each tile closely for any ascender, abbreviation stroke or word shape and found none I could defend even as an uncertain reading. I have not written any conjectural letters, because anything I offered would be invention.

Limitations and what would help
- No single word or letter is read; this packet cannot support a source match from my reading.
- The blur is in the object, not the image resolution: the tiles are sharp on the parchment grain.
- Useful next steps: raking light, UV or infrared/multispectral imaging of the strip; a transmitted-light image if the strip is lifted; a mirrored and contrast-stretched version of image-006 (if the writing is show-through it will be mirror-reversed); and an image of the spine face of the strip, which no tile here shows squarely.
